title: Kyoya and Train
statementMd:
Kyoya Ootori wants to take the train to get to school. There are $*n*$ train stations and $*m*$ one-way train lines going between various stations. Kyoya is currently at train station $1$, and the school is at station $*n*$. To take a train, he must pay for a ticket, and the train also takes a certain amount of time. However, the trains are not perfect and take random amounts of time to arrive at their destination. If Kyoya arrives at school strictly after $*t*$ time units, he will have to pay a fine of $*x*$.

Each train line is described by a ticket price, and a probability distribution on the time the train takes. More formally, train line $*i*$ has ticket cost $*c*_{*i*}$, and a probability distribution $*p*_{*i*, *k*}$ which denotes the probability that this train will take $*k*$ time units for all $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *t*$. Amounts of time that each of the trains used by Kyouya takes are mutually independent random values (moreover, if Kyoya travels along the same train more than once, it is possible for the train to take different amounts of time and those amounts are also independent one from another).

Kyoya wants to get to school by spending the least amount of money in expectation (for the ticket price plus possible fine for being late). Of course, Kyoya has an optimal plan for how to get to school, and every time he arrives at a train station, he may recalculate his plan based on how much time he has remaining. What is the expected cost that Kyoya will pay to get to school if he moves optimally?

## Input

The first line of input contains four integers $*n*, *m*, *t*, *x*$ ($2  ≤  *n*  ≤ 50$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ 100$, $1 ≤ *t* ≤ 20 000$, $0 ≤ *x* ≤ 10^{6}$).

The next $2*m*$ lines contain the description of the trains.

The $2*i*$-th line will have $3$ integers $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}$, representing a one way train from station $*a*_{*i*}$ to $*b*_{*i*}$ with ticket cost $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*_{*i*}$, $0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$). There will always be at least one path from any station to the school.

The $(2*i* + 1)$-th line will contain $*t*$ integers, $*p*_{*i*, 1}, *p*_{*i*, 2}, ..., *p*_{*i*, *t*}$ where $*p*_{*i*, *k*} / 100000$ is the probability that this train will take $*k*$ units of time to traverse ($0 ≤ *p*_{*i*, *k*} ≤ 100 000$ for $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *t*$, ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1dd6644a681804a6c6570ab0c07a69e19b83516c.png)).

It is guaranteed that there is no more than one train between each pair of platforms in each of the directions.

## Output

Print a single real number that is equal to an optimal expected cost of getting to school. The answer will be considered correct if its relative or absolute error doesn't exceed $10^{ - 6}$.

## Note

The optimal strategy in the first case is as follows:

First, travel along first train line. With probability $1 / 2$ Kyoya will take $1$ time unit. Otherwise, Kyoya will take $3$ time units.

If the train takes $1$ time unit, travel along the 4th train line. Kyoya will make it to school in time with probability $1 / 2$. Otherwise, if the train takes 3 time units, travel along the 2nd train line. Kyoya will make it to school in time with probability $1 / 10$.

Since the cost of all train lines are zero, we can just look at the probability that Kyoya will incur the penalty. The probability that Kyoya will have to pay the penalty is $1 / 2 × 1 / 2 + 1 / 2 × 9 / 10 = 7 / 10$. We can show that no other strategy is strictly better.

The optimal strategy in the second case is to travel along $1 → 2 → 4$ no matter what. Kyoya will incur the penalty with probability $3 / 4$, and the cost of the trains is $200$, thus the expected cost is $200.75$.
statementZhMd:
Kyoya Ootori 想乘坐列车去学校。有 $*n*$ 个火车站，以及连接各个车站的 $*m*$ 条单向列车线路。Kyoya 当前位于 1 号车站，学校位于 $*n*$ 号车站。乘坐列车需要支付车票费用，同时列车也需要花费一定的时间。然而，列车并不总是准时，抵达目的地所需的时间是随机的。如果 Kyoya 严格晚于 $*t*$ 个时间单位到达学校，他将被罚款 $*x*$。

每条列车线路由车票价格以及列车运行时间的概率分布描述。更正式地说，第 $*i*$ 条列车线路的票价为 $*c*_{*i*}$，并且有一个概率分布 $*p*_{*i*, *k*}$，表示对于所有 $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *t*$，该列车需要 $*k*$ 个时间单位的概率。Kyoya 乘坐的各趟列车所花费的时间相互独立（此外，如果 Kyoya 多次乘坐同一列车，该列车每次也可能花费不同的时间，并且这些时间彼此独立）。

Kyoya 希望使到达学校所需的期望花费（车票费用加上可能产生的迟到罚款）最小。当然，Kyoya 有一个到达学校的最优方案，并且每当他到达一个车站时，都可以根据剩余时间重新规划方案。如果他采取最优行动，那么到达学校时需要支付的期望费用是多少？

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含四个整数 $*n*, *m*, *t*, *x*$（$2  ≤  *n*  ≤ 50$，$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 100$，$1 ≤ *t* ≤ 20\,000$，$0 ≤ *x* ≤ 10^{6}$）。

接下来的 $2*m*$ 行包含列车的描述。

第 $2*i*$ 行包含 $3$ 个整数 $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}$，表示一条从车站 $*a*_{*i*}$ 前往车站 $*b*_{*i*}$ 的单向列车线路，其票价为 $*c*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*a*_{*i*} ≠ *b*_{*i*}$，$0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$）。保证从任意车站都至少存在一条通往学校的路径。

第 $(2*i* + 1)$ 行包含 $*t*$ 个整数 $*p*_{*i*, 1}, *p*_{*i*, 2}, ..., *p*_{*i*, *t*}$，其中 $*p*_{*i*, *k*} / 100000$ 是该列车运行 $*k*$ 个时间单位的概率（$0 ≤ *p*_{*i*, *k*} ≤ 100 000$，对于 $1 ≤ *k* ≤ *t*$，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1dd6644a681804a6c6570ab0c07a69e19b83516c.png)）。

保证任意两个车站之间，在每个方向上至多有一条列车线路。

## 输出格式

输出一个实数，表示到达学校的最优期望费用。如果答案的相对误差或绝对误差不超过 $10^{ - 6}$，则视为正确。

## 说明

第一种情况的最优策略如下：

首先，乘坐第一条列车线路。Kyoya 以 $1 / 2$ 的概率花费 $1$ 个时间单位到达；否则，他将花费 $3$ 个时间单位。

如果列车花费了 $1$ 个时间单位，则乘坐第 4 条列车线路。Kyoya 以 $1 / 2$ 的概率及时到达学校。否则，如果列车花费了 $3$ 个时间单位，则乘坐第 2 条列车线路。此时 Kyoya 及时到达学校的概率为 $1 / 10$。

由于所有列车线路的费用均为零，我们只需考虑 Kyoya 需要支付罚款的概率。Kyoya 需要支付罚款的概率为 $1 / 2 × 1 / 2 + 1 / 2 × 9 / 10 = 7 / 10$。可以证明，没有其他策略会严格优于该策略。

第二种情况的最优策略是无论发生什么都沿着 $1 → 2 → 4$ 行驶。Kyoya 以 $3 / 4$ 的概率需要支付罚款，列车费用为 $200$，因此期望费用为 $200.75$。
